subject: Request: Temporary deviation to P1/P2 response windows and escalation contacts
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@tideways.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: support@tideways.ai, procurement@tideways.ai
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary P2 extension + on-call escalation for migration weekend

Jonas —

Hope you’re well. We’re kicking a large data migration and load test this Friday 9/24 through Sunday 9/26 (US-Pacific) as part of our go-live. The migration will generate a high volume of non-user-impacting alerts while our internal ops team runs the cutover, and several of our engineers will be out monitoring in the field.

Two asks:
- For the migration window (72h maximum), can Redwood temporarily extend our P2 response window from 4 hours to 8 hours? We only need this for lower-severity noisy alerts while the cutover is active.
- Can you provide a named escalation contact and a dedicated on-call bridge (single point of contact) so we can route critical P1s directly if anything user-impacting occurs? We want to avoid delays if a real outage happens.

If possible please also confirm whether a credit would apply for any P1/P2 SLA breaches during the window given the planned test load. We can sign a short amendment to the current SLA for the 72h carveout. I’ve cc’d procurement to track paperwork.

I attached a short runbook excerpt that shows our planned cutover timeline and typical alert noise patterns.

Thanks — appreciate quick confirmation so we can finalize our calendar and on-call rotation.

—Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Platform Operations, Tideways
elena@tideways.ai | +1 415-555-0138

Attachment: tideways-runbook-troubleshooting.pdf (excerpt)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morales <elena@tideways.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, support@tideways.ai
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary P2 extension + on-call escalation for migration weekend

Elena —

Thanks for the heads-up and the runbook excerpt. We can accommodate a short, scoped deviation but need to lock a few items before approving an amendment. High level response:

Proposed Redwood response/compromise:
- Scope: one 48-hour carveout (we can extend to 72h subject to final review).
- P2 window: extend from 4h -> 8h for the carveout window only.
- P1 window: we cannot relax P1 guarantees — we will provide a named escalation contact and a dedicated on-call bridge to ensure P1s—our target P1 response remains 1 hour.
- Credits: if a P1 SLA breach occurs during the carveout for reasons attributable to Redwood, standard SLA crediting applies. For noisier P2 churn we won’t issue credits where the event is expected due to the planned migration (we’ll document this in the amendment).

Action items we need from Tideways to proceed:
1) Confirm exact start/end timestamps for the carveout (UTC).
2) Share an up-to-date runbook (the excerpt is helpful but we need the full section that lists alert signatures and throttling rules).
3) Confirm the primary Tideways on-call person during the window and the phone/bridge number you want us to use.

If you approve, we’ll prepare a one-page SLA amendment and a mutual action plan (MAP) that includes the dedicated bridge number and the named Redwood on-call engineer. I’m cc’ing KarTHIK to propose an internal owner for the bridge and Marissa to loop in Customer Success for the contract changes.

Jonas Weber
Sr. Account Manager — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai | +1 617-555-0220

Elena / Jonas —

Quick technical note from infra: we can instantiate a dedicated escalation bridge and enable an aggressive alert-suppression filter scoped to Tideways during the migration window. Proposed operational details: 

- Bridge: we will spin up a dedicated conference bridge and pager routing to a named Redwood engineer for the window. Proposed primary Redwood on-call: Karthik Iyer (karthik_iyer@redwood.ai). Backup: Marissa Cole (marissa_cole@redwood.ai).
- Bridge number + SIP: we’ll provide the dial-in and SIP address once you confirm the final timestamps.
- Monitoring tweaks: we’ll apply a temporary prefix filter for common migration noise (keys: auth-temp-fail, kv-cache-warm, model-load-spikes). This will reduce false P1 escalations while preserving real user-impacting signals.
- Rollback: filter changes are reversible within 10 minutes; we’ll maintain a live runbook entry and write the exact commands applied.

I’ve attached an internal runbook fragment we propose adding to your document to show what we’ll do. Please confirm: start 2027-09-25T00:00:00Z -> end 2027-09-27T00:00:00Z (48h). If you need 72h we can extend but need procurement signoff this week.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
